title: Clinical Quality and Durability of Posterior Resin Composite Restorations After 28 Years: An In Vivo Study
summary:
Composites are currently the predominant material for direct dental restorations in most countries. Tooth-colored resin-based materials offer several advantages, including favorable esthetics, tissue conservation, and good clinical long-term performance—even in posterior teeth. However, a variety of factors, such as cavity size, tooth type, and patient-related factors, can influence the quality and longevity of these restorations.

This clinical follow-up observational study evaluates posterior composite restorations placed between 1995 and 1996 by dental students at the University Dental Institute in Frankfurt am Main (Carolinum), following a standardized clinical protocol. A first follow-up was conducted between 6 and 36 months after placement. A second follow-up took place over 23 years later, in 2019. Now, a third follow-up is being performed approximately 28 years after the initial restorations.

The aim of this study is to assess the long-term quality of these restorations under real-world clinical conditions using standardized and internationally comparable evaluation criteria (modified FDI criteria), and to compare the findings with earlier results and international studies. In addition, subgroup differences (e.g., molars vs. premolars; single-surface vs. multi-surface restorations; maxilla vs. mandible) will be analyzed.

Hypotheses:

    The quality scores of the restorations after 28 years show a statistically significant deterioration compared to earlier follow-ups.

    Some of the original restorations have since been repaired, replaced, received prosthetic treatment, or the tooth has been lost.

    Multi-surface restorations and restorations in molars tend to show significantly lower ratings than single-surface restorations or premolars.
conditions: Long-term performance of composite restorations in structural defects of the hard dental tissues in posterior teeth

interventions.name:
Clinical follow-up observational study evaluating posterior composite restorations placed with Herculite XRV during student training courses at the Department of Operative Dentistry, University Clinic Frankfurt am Main in the years 1995–1996.

These restorations were assessed in a first follow-up

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. The placement of the posterior composite restorations was carried out during the undergraduate clinical courses in Operative Dentistry at the Goethe University Frankfurt am Main, Germany, in 1995/1996.
2. All restorations were placed in permanent, vital teeth that showed no pain symptoms at the time of treatment.
3. A microhybrid composite (Herculite XRV, Kerr, Karlsruhe, Germany) was used for the restorations.
4. The application followed a predefined clinical protocol.
5. All patients were between 18 and 70 years old at the time of restoration placement.
6. All patients were re-examined during the first follow-up between 1995 and 1997, within 36 months after the initial placement of the restorations.
Exclusion criteria:
1. The placement of the posterior composite restorations did not take place during the undergraduate clinical courses in Operative Dentistry at Goethe University Frankfurt am Main, Germany, in 1995/1996.
2. The restorations were not placed in permanent, vital teeth that were free of pain symptoms at the time of treatment.
3. A microhybrid composite (Herculite XRV, Kerr, Karlsruhe, Germany) was not used for the restorations.
4. The application did not follow a predefined clinical protocol.
5. The patients were not between 18 and 70 years of age at the time of restoration placement.
6. The patients were not re-examined during the first follow-up between 1995 and 1997 within 36 months after the initial placement of the restorations.
